title: The Obex Artifact may not be amended in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas, and enforcing that is a named duty
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 states: "The Obex Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals."

This establishes a genuine constitutional hierarchy rather than a federation of peers. An Agent Artifact is a subordinate document, and no amount of token holder support can lift it above the Atlas. Sky Governance therefore does not need to review each Agent amendment — the limit is built into what an amendment can be.

The restriction has three layers of increasing looseness: violating the Atlas itself, violating the Atlas's specifications of the Sky Primitives, or being "otherwise misaligned." The third is open-textured by design, extending the limit past anything textually enumerated to the spirit-of-the-rule reading the Atlas relies on elsewhere.

Enforcement is where the design becomes fragile. The rule is stated as an absolute constraint on what the Artifact *can be*, but the only mechanism named for upholding it is the Operational Facilitator's review. There is no ratification step, no Sky-side veto, and no stated remedy if a violating edit nonetheless passes — so a substantive constraint of constitutional force rests entirely on one role performing one review correctly.
description: A substantive limit sits above the procedural one: edits violating the Atlas, its Primitive specifications, or that are "otherwise misaligned" are void regardless of vote outcome.
